。沒有譜的時候，團體靠事先講好的幾條規則運作：誰先開始、什麼訊號代表轉段、什麼時: . When there is no score, the group runs on a few rules agreed in advance: who starts, which signal means a change of section, when everyone stops, how long each person may keep going at a time. These rules are usually minimal — for instance "anyone who starts a new note, everyone else has to move to another note within a very short time", or "you may only sound in the gaps where someone else has stopped". The function of the rules is not to decide the music but to let the music turn a corner with nobody conducting.
傳統合奏排練是把同一段反覆練到整齊；這裡的排練更像是建立共同詞彙：確認某個手勢代: A traditional ensemble rehearsal repeats the same passage until it is tidy; rehearsal here is more like building a shared vocabulary: confirming what a certain gesture means, what the others should do when a certain sound appears, in what circumstances the rules may be broken. A lot of time goes on listening and discussion rather than playing. At the first rehearsal of a new work, reading through the instructions and clearing up the uncertain places often takes a long while, and the actual playing is brief. This kind of rehearsal looks inefficient, yet it is the only workable method for this line-up: if the agreements are not clear, there is nothing to lean on once you are on stage.
先確認「這一場的規則」。節目單或開場說明通常會講作品靠什麼運作，知道規則是聽懂的: First find out the rules of this performance. The programme note or the spoken introduction usually says what the work runs on, and knowing the rules is the precondition for following it.
出現在美術館、藝術節、小型音樂廳、教堂、倉庫與非典型場地。曲目包含圖形譜作品、文: It appears in museums, festivals, small concert halls, churches, warehouses and unusual venues. The repertoire includes graphic-score works, text-score works, installation-style performances written for a particular site, and improvisation structures the group has developed on its own. Lengths vary widely, from a dozen minutes to several hours; some works are installation states the audience can walk in and out of, rather than concerts with a clear beginning and end.
和世界音樂樂團相比，差別在改編的目的。世界音樂樂團要讓不同傳統的樂器在同一個調與: Compared with a world music ensemble, the difference is the purpose of adaptation. A world music ensemble wants instruments from different traditions to coexist in one key and one beat, and its core work is translation and compromise; an experimental sound collective does not seek coexistence. It lets sounds from different sources keep their own texture, and uses agreements to decide when they appear and when they give way.
噪音是材料之一，但團體同樣處理時間、密度、讓位與結束。差別在於判斷標準不是音高與: Noise is one of the materials, but the group still handles time, density, giving way and ending. The difference is that the criteria are texture and structure, not pitch and harmony.
在持續層上放置短促、可辨認的動作: Places short, recognisable actions on top of the sustain layer
在這裡不是裝飾，而是主要的聲音來源。傳統樂器被要求做出它原本不被期待的聲音：在琴: , here, is not decoration but the main source of sound. Traditional instruments are asked for sounds they were not expected to make: bowing behind the bridge, drawing the bow across the edge of a cymbal, putting objects between the piano strings, speaking into a pipe instead of blowing it. Most of these techniques have no standard notation and are passed on only by demonstration and word of mouth. When someone joins the group, what they learn is not a score but the details of these actions: how slow the bow, how light the pressure, which spot produces which harmonic.
實驗聲響團體不演奏「真正的音樂」，只是製造噪音。: An experimental sound collective does not play "real music"; it just makes noise.
實驗聲響團體（Experimental Sound Collective）— 以: Experimental Sound Collective — a sound group working from graphic scores, verbal instructions and improvisation agreements, settling things on the spot rather than rehearsing a fixed version. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
實驗聲響團體（experimental sound collective）是二十: The experimental sound collective is a playing group that formed in contemporary art circles in Europe, North America and Japan from the mid-twentieth century onward, its members drawn from performance, composition, sound art and the visual arts. It plays to museums, festivals and small venues, and its works often have no traditional score, existing instead as graphics, texts or spoken agreements. The line-up holds together because a body of work cannot be fully expressed on the five-line staff and has to be settled by a group of people on the spot.

常介於語言與聲音之間: Often somewhere between language and sound
延伸技法對控制的要求很高：弓速、壓力、位置稍有不同，聲音就完全不同。技巧沒有消失: Extended technique demands a great deal of control: change the bow speed, the pressure or the contact point even slightly and the sound is completely different. The technique has not gone away; it simply is not written in the score.
弦樂長音、風琴、電子持續音: Long string tones, organ, electronic drones
把上述聲音重新分配與變形: Redistributes and transforms the sounds above
排練的方式也跟著改變。: The way of rehearsing changes too.
接受不確定。同一件作品聽兩次不會一樣，這不是演奏失誤，而是記譜方式本身的結果。: Accept uncertainty. The same work will not be the same twice, and that is not a mistake in playing but a result of how it is notated.
提供時間的底，讓其他事件有參照: Gives the floor of time so other events have a reference
提供無法記譜的聲響質地: Provides sound textures that cannot be notated
最容易和電子原聲混合編制搞混。兩者都在當代藝術場館演出，也都不靠傳統總譜；差別在: The easiest confusion is with the electroacoustic ensemble. Both perform in contemporary art venues and both work without a traditional score; the difference is the form of the agreement and who decides. In the electroacoustic ensemble the time is held up by fixed tracks, a click or processing parameters, the sound engineer is a member, and part of the work's sound is written into the system; the experimental sound collective uses graphic scores, text scores or verbal rules, the decisions are spread among the players, and the sound engineer is usually just one of the operators. One puts the structure into the equipment, the other puts it into people's judgement.
有些團體規定只有一個人能觸發轉段，其他人負責跟隨；有些團體則規定任何人的動作都可: Some groups rule that only one person can trigger a change of section and the others follow; others rule that anyone's action can become the turn and the others must judge whether to follow. The first is close to having a conductor, except that the conductor works by hints rather than gestures; the second asks everyone to switch constantly between listening and deciding. Each has its price: the first is stable but slow to react, the second is flexible but easily loses control. Groups usually choose one according to the work and the venue rather than fixing on one for good.
歐美・當代藝術: Europe and North America · contemporary art
沒有傳統總譜，但有圖形、文字或口頭規則。約束還在，只是換了形式；演奏者要做的是在: There is no traditional score, but there are graphics, texts or spoken rules. The constraints are still there, only in another form; what the player has to do is judge inside them, not do whatever comes to mind.
沒有譜就等於隨便演奏。: No score means playing whatever you like.
注意無聲的段落。停頓在這個編制裡是結構的一部分，不是冷場。: Notice the silent passages. In this line-up a pause is part of the structure, not an awkward gap.
當作品在美術館或非典型場地演出，觀眾會走動、會進出、會發出聲音。團體必須把這些納: When a work is performed in a museum or an unusual venue, the audience walks about, comes and goes, makes noise. The group has to take this into its judgement: a quiet passage may be filled with footsteps, a long tone may be buried by the noise of the room. Some works deliberately write the audience's behaviour into the instructions, making the audience one of the sources of uncertainty.
當沒有譜也沒有指揮，團體實際同意的是「如何開始、如何結束、如何讓位」。: With no score and no conductor, what the group actually agrees on is how to start, how to end and how to give way.
約定也包含「誰可以改變狀態」。: The agreements also cover who is allowed to change the state.
維持約定、給提示、決定何時開始與結束: Holds the agreements, gives cues, decides when to start and when to end
編制不固定，以十人以下的小型組合為主，樂器可以是傳統樂器、自製樂器、電子設備、日: The line-up is not fixed; it is usually a small group of fewer than ten, and the instruments can be traditional instruments, home-made instruments, electronic equipment, everyday objects or the voice. The division of work is not by section either, but by who is responsible for which kind of action: someone for long sustained tones, someone for triggering events, someone for operating the equipment.
聽持續層。實驗聲響不是一連串事件，通常有一條長音或噪音在底下撐著，事件才有位置。: Listen to the sustain layer. Experimental sound is not a string of events; there is usually a long tone or a noise holding things up underneath, and that is what gives the events a place to sit.
聽空間。很多作品是為特定場地的殘響寫的，換場地就換了一個版本。: Listen to the space. Many works are written for the reverb of a particular venue, and changing venue makes it a different version.
與爵士小編制相比，差別在即興的規則從哪裡來。爵士的即興建立在共用的和聲進行與律動: Compared with a jazz combo, the difference is where the rules of improvisation come from. Jazz improvisation is built on shared chord progressions and a groove, and the players know when their turn comes; experimental improvisation is built on agreements accumulated inside the group over time. Those agreements may be adjusted for the venue and the work, but they have no cross-style common standard the way jazz harmony does.
觀眾的位置也是結構的一部分。: The audience's position is part of the structure too.
這三件事比音符更重要。開始得太突然，聲音會沒有參照；結束得不乾脆，殘響會拖住整段: These three matter more than the notes. If you start too suddenly the sound has no reference; if you do not end cleanly the reverb drags the whole passage; if you do not give way everyone fills the spectrum at once and the sound becomes one mass. Experienced groups rehearse these three things over and over rather than rehearsing a particular passage. That is also why the same group sounds so different from venue to venue: the length of the room's reverb changes how long giving way takes.
這些角色常由同一個人兼任。一個弦樂手可能同時操作效果器，一個打擊手可能同時負責計: These roles are often held by the same person. A string player may also operate effects, a percussionist may also keep the time. The blurring of the line-up is deliberate: it lets the group adjust to the venue and the work without forming a new ensemble for every new piece.
這個編制的核心問題是: The central question of this line-up is—
這種音樂不需要技巧。: This kind of music needs no technique.
通常是發起人，不一定是指揮: Usually the person who initiated the work; not necessarily a conductor
（graphic score）。譜面上畫的不是音符，而是線條、色塊、箭頭、方格。: . What is drawn on the page is not notes but lines, blocks of colour, arrows and boxes. A rising curve may mean the pitch rising, a slowly growing circle may mean the volume growing, dense dots may mean short bursts of sound. The advantage of a graphic score is that it holds what the staff cannot write — slides, noise, uncertain pitch; the price is that its meaning is not fixed. Two people can read the same drawing as two different performances. So a graphic score almost always comes with a set of spoken instructions, or relies on a consensus built up inside the group.
（text score）。整首作品由一段文字構成，指示演奏者做什麼：在室內某個位: . A whole work is made of a paragraph of text telling the player what to do: how long to stand at a certain spot in the room, what to listen to, under what condition to start, under what condition to stop. A text score widens "playing" into "behaving", and sometimes produces no sound in the traditional sense at all. It forces the player to judge the details, and makes the same work different at every performance.
